nahw.meaning: a ẓarf of time, such as <bdi>أَمْسِ</bdi>, yesterday
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: a ẓarf of place, such as <bdi>خَلْفَ</bdi>, behind
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: isms that stand in for something left unnamed: an amount, or words and events
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09
Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: What two jobs can <bdi>كَمْ</bdi> do?
nahw.back: Ask: <bdi>كَمْ كِتَابًا قَرَأْتَ؟</bdi>, “how many books did you read?” Or exclaim: <bdi>كَمْ كِتَابٍ قَرَأْتُ!</bdi>, “how many a book I've read!”
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: so many, so much — such-and-such an amount: <bdi>عِنْدِي كَذَا دِرْهَمًا</bdi>, I have such-and-such dirhams
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: such and such — standing in for words or events, like <bdi>ذَيْتَ وَذَيْتَ</bdi>: <bdi>قَالَ كَيْتَ وَكَيْتَ</bdi>, he said such and such
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Among the <bdi>كِنَايَات</bdi>, what do <bdi>كَمْ</bdi> and <bdi>كَذَا</bdi> stand in for, and what do <bdi>كَيْتَ</bdi> and <bdi>ذَيْتَ</bdi>?
nahw.back: An unnamed amount; unnamed words or events
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: What are the two kinds of muʿrab ism, and which is the default?
nahw.back: <bdi>مُنْصَرِف</bdi> and <bdi>غَيْر مُنْصَرِف</bdi>. An ism is munṣarif unless a cause makes it otherwise.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: fully declinable: a muʿrab ism that takes tanwīn and all three endings, like <bdi>كِتَابٌ</bdi>, <bdi>كِتَابًا</bdi>, <bdi>كِتَابٍ</bdi>
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: partly declinable: a muʿrab ism that never takes tanwīn or a kasrah
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.text: A <bdi>غَيْر مُنْصَرِف</bdi> ism shows rafʿ with {{c1::a ḍammah}}, naṣb with {{c2::a fatḥah}} and jarr with {{c3::a fatḥah, in place of the kasrah}} — and never takes tanwīn
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: What does <bdi>الصَّرْف</bdi> mean in <bdi>المَمْنُوع مِنَ الصَّرْف</bdi>?
nahw.back: Tanwīn, not the science of ṣarf: the word is “barred from tanwīn”
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: When does a ghayr munṣarif ism take a kasrah after all?
nahw.back: When it has <bdi>ال</bdi> or is muḍāf: <bdi>فِي المَسَاجِدِ</bdi> (2:187), <bdi>فِي أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ</bdi> (95:4)
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: How many causes does it take to make an ism ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: One strong cause, or two weak causes together. A strong cause counts as two on its own.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: What are the two strong causes, each enough on its own to make an ism ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: Being a <bdi>جَمْع مُنْتَهَى الجُمُوع</bdi>, and ending in an alif of taʾnīth
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: the “ultimate plural”: a broken plural shaped like <bdi>مَفَاعِل</bdi> or <bdi>مَفَاعِيل</bdi>, such as <bdi>مَسَاجِد</bdi> and <bdi>مَفَاتِيح</bdi>
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.text: After its alif of the plural, a <bdi>جَمْع مُنْتَهَى الجُمُوع</bdi> has one of three things: {{c1::two vowelled letters}}, {{c2::one doubled letter}}, or {{c3::three letters, the middle one sākin}}
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: How does <bdi>مَصَابِيح</bdi> appear in <bdi>وَلَقَدْ زَيَّنَّا السَّمَاءَ الدُّنْيَا بِمَصَابِيحَ</bdi> (67:5), and why?
nahw.back: With a fatḥah and no tanwīn, though it's majrūr after <bdi>بِ</bdi>. It's a <bdi>جَمْع مُنْتَهَى الجُمُوع</bdi>: three letters follow the alif, the middle one sākin.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Which sign of femininity is a strong cause on its own, and in what two forms does it come?
nahw.back: The alif of taʾnīth. Maqṣūrah, with no hamzah after it: <bdi>ذِكْرَى</bdi>, <bdi>حُبْلَى</bdi>. Or mamdūdah, followed by a hamzah: <bdi>صَحْرَاء</bdi>, <bdi>حَمْرَاء</bdi>. It counts whether or not the word is a name, or feminine in meaning.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: <bdi>مَدْرَسَةٌ</bdi> ends in a sign of femininity, yet it takes tanwīn. Why?
nahw.back: A tāʾ marbūṭah is only a weak cause, so it needs a second: being a name, as in <bdi>فَاطِمَةُ</bdi>. Only the alif of taʾnīth is strong enough alone.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: A word ending in an alif maqṣūrah hides all its endings anyway. How can you tell a ghayr munṣarif one from a munṣarif one?
nahw.back: By tanwīn. A munṣarif one takes it when indefinite: <bdi>فَتًى</bdi>, <bdi>هُدًى</bdi>. A ghayr munṣarif one never does: <bdi>ذِكْرَى</bdi>, <bdi>حُبْلَى</bdi>.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: How must two weak causes pair up to make an ism ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: One of meaning — being a name or a descriptor — with one of form
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: being a proper name — one of the two weak causes of meaning
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: being a descriptor, an adjective — one of the two weak causes of meaning
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.text: The six weak causes of form: {{c1::taʾnīth without the alif — a tāʾ marbūṭah, or a feminine meaning}}, {{c2::being non-Arabic}}, {{c3::being a compound}}, {{c4::an added alif and nūn}}, {{c5::a verb's pattern}} and {{c6::having left its original form}}
nahw.extra: In Arabic: <bdi>التَّأْنِيث</bdi>, <bdi>العُجْمَة</bdi>, <bdi>التَّرْكِيب</bdi>, <bdi>الأَلِف وَالنُّون الزَّائِدَتَان</bdi>, <bdi>وَزْن الفِعْل</bdi> and <bdi>العَدْل</bdi>.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: A tāʾ marbūṭah, or a feminine meaning: which cause of meaning must it pair with, and what are examples?
nahw.back: Only being a name. By the tāʾ: <bdi>فَاطِمَة</bdi>, <bdi>طَلْحَة</bdi>, <bdi>مَكَّة</bdi>. By meaning: <bdi>زَيْنَب</bdi>, <bdi>مَرْيَم</bdi>.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: being non-Arabic — a weak cause of form that pairs only with being a name, as in <bdi>إِبْرَاهِيم</bdi> and <bdi>يُوسُف</bdi>
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: <bdi>إِبْرَاهِيم</bdi> is ghayr munṣarif as a non-Arabic name. Why do <bdi>نُوح</bdi> and <bdi>لُوط</bdi> still take tanwīn?
nahw.back: A three-letter name with a sākin middle letter is light enough to stay munṣarif: <bdi>وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا</bdi> (11:25)
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: being a compound: two words fused into one name, such as <bdi>حَضْرَمَوْت</bdi> and <bdi>بَعْلَبَكّ</bdi> — a weak cause of form, only for names
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: An added alif and nūn: which causes of meaning can it pair with, and what are examples?
nahw.back: Either. A name: <bdi>عُثْمَان</bdi>, <bdi>مَرْوَان</bdi>. A descriptor on <bdi>فَعْلَان</bdi>: <bdi>سَكْرَان</bdi>, <bdi>غَضْبَان</bdi>. The two letters must be added, not part of the root.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: A verb's pattern: which causes of meaning can it pair with, and what are examples?
nahw.back: Either. A name: <bdi>يَزِيد</bdi>, <bdi>يَثْرِب</bdi>. A descriptor on <bdi>أَفْعَل</bdi>: <bdi>أَحْمَر</bdi>, <bdi>أَكْبَر</bdi>.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.meaning: an ism having left its original form, as <bdi>عُمَر</bdi> is said to come from <bdi>عَامِر</bdi> — a weak cause of form
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why did the grammarians posit <bdi>العَدْل</bdi>?
nahw.back: Names like <bdi>عُمَر</bdi> and <bdi>زُفَر</bdi> never take tanwīn, yet show only one cause: being a name. So the grammarians judged that such a word must have left an original form, and counted that as its second cause.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>أَحْمَد</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: Two weak causes: it's a name, and it's on a verb's pattern
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>أَفْضَل</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: Two weak causes: it's a descriptor, and it's on a verb's pattern (<bdi>أَفْعَل</bdi>)
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>حَمْزَة</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: Two weak causes: it's a name, and it ends in a tāʾ marbūṭah — though it names a man
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>سُعَاد</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: Two weak causes: it's a name, and it's feminine in meaning
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>إِسْمَاعِيل</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: Two weak causes: it's a name, and it's non-Arabic
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why does <bdi>رَمَضَان</bdi> end in a fatḥah in <bdi>شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ</bdi> (2:185), though it's a muḍāf ilayhi?
nahw.back: It's ghayr munṣarif by two weak causes — a name, with an added alif and nūn — so its jarr shows as a fatḥah
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>عَطْشَان</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: Two weak causes: it's a descriptor, with an added alif and nūn (<bdi>فَعْلَان</bdi>)
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>عُلَمَاء</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: One strong cause: it ends in an alif mamdūdah of taʾnīth — though it isn't feminine in meaning
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: Why is <bdi>دَرَاهِم</bdi> ghayr munṣarif?
nahw.back: One strong cause: it's a <bdi>جَمْع مُنْتَهَى الجُمُوع</bdi>, with two vowelled letters after the alif
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09

nahw.front: <bdi>مُحَمَّدٌ</bdi> is a name. Why does it still take tanwīn?
nahw.back: Being a name is only one weak cause, of meaning. With no cause of form beside it, the word stays munṣarif.
nahw.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-11-09
